# Summarise, tag and file every link with the owner's own AI key

## Intent

A library of hundreds of links is only navigable if each one says what it is. This package has every fetched link summarised, tagged and given a topic by an AI provider, running only on the key the owner has entered themselves (Anthropic by default, or OpenRouter), with a vocabulary of tags and topics that converges instead of fragmenting, background work paced so that large batches never flood the provider, failures and rejected keys reported plainly, and the owner's own edits of title, summary, tags and topic always winning over anything automatic. Without a key, the library works fully and simply leaves links unenriched.

## Goals

- For a reachable page and a user with a verified key, the card shows title, summary, tags and topic without reload within 60 seconds of the link being added.
- Enrichment runs only with the user's own AI provider key, entered once in settings; without one, everything else works and links are simply not enriched.
- The stored key is encrypted at rest and never shown again beyond its last 4 characters, nor returned by any API response.
- Imports and "enrich all" never process more than 20 links per minute per user.
- A field the owner has edited is never overwritten by later enrichment or re-fetch.

## Non-goals

- Fetching, snapshots and the reader view: package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`), whose reader-view text this package reads.
- The Topics and Tags pages, renaming and merging topics and tags, and search over summary, tags and topic: package 06 (`search_and_browse`).
- Bulk import: package 07 (`bulk_import`), which schedules its fetches through this package's throttle. Export of tags, topics and summaries: package 09; the AI key is never exported.
- A shared or deployment-wide AI key, and Workers AI as a provider: rejected by the owner (source PRD decisions 5 and 9).
- Re-enriching existing links when the provider, model or key changes.
- Semantic / vector search.

## Background

Package 01 (`accounts_links_and_stream`) provides the users, links, the API conventions (error envelope, 409 limits, 429 rate limits, the OpenAPI document kept in step with the routes), the settings page, the stream card `LinkCard.tsx`, the link detail page and the test helpers. Package 02 (`fetch_and_snapshot`) fetches each link through `FETCH_QUEUE` and its consumer (the fetch worker), stores the reader-view text in `link_texts` (empty when extraction yields under 200 characters), the title and description on the link, notes such as "not a web page", "no text in this PDF" and "PDF too large to store (50 MB limit)", refreshes a link on request, and updates the stream in place by polling `GET /api/v1/links?changed_since=` while a card is pending or refreshing. Nothing yet produces a summary, tags or a topic.

Constraints the owner has set:

- Constraint: **bring your own key.** Enrichment is only ever run with an AI provider key the user has entered on the settings page. Each user chooses a provider, the **Anthropic Claude API** (default, through the official `@anthropic-ai/sdk`) or **OpenRouter** (through its API, so any model it hosts can be used), enters their API key, and optionally a model identifier (default `claude-opus-5-5` for Anthropic; for OpenRouter the user must name a model).
- Constraint: page text sent to the provider is the cleaned reader-view text, truncated to the first 20,000 characters, never the raw HTML, cookies or the user's identity. The provider is called with the user's key and nothing shared between users.
- Constraint: strict per-user separation of data and processing.

## Requirements

### AI provider and key

- On the settings page the user chooses the provider (Anthropic, the default, or OpenRouter), enters their API key and optionally a model identifier (default `claude-opus-5-5` for Anthropic; for OpenRouter a model is required). Saving the key runs a test request; a key the provider rejects is refused with the provider's message and not stored, and the page says "key verified" for one it accepts. The stored key is encrypted at rest, shown only as its last 4 characters afterwards, can be replaced or removed, and is never included in the export, the API or MCP responses. Changing provider, model or key does not re-enrich existing links.

### Enrichment

- Enrichment: from the cleaned text, an LLM produces a summary of at most 60 words, 3 to 8 tags (lower-case, single words or hyphenated phrases), and one topic. Tags and topic are drawn from the user's existing tags and topics where one fits and new ones are created where none does, so that vocabulary converges rather than fragments. These are stored on the link and shown in the stream.
- From a PDF, enrichment runs on its extracted text as for a page; a PDF with no extractable text, a link that is not a web page and a PDF too large to store are not enriched. When the reader view yields fewer than 200 characters, enrichment uses the page title and description only.
- Without a stored key, fetch and snapshot run as normal and every link skips enrichment; the stream shows such links with "not enriched: add an AI key in settings" once as a banner, not per link. When a key is added later, the user can trigger "enrich all unenriched links" from settings, which processes them at the background rate below.
- Background processing (imports and "enrich all") runs at no more than 20 links per minute per user (a 600-link batch completes in about 30 minutes).
- Failures: when enrichment fails (provider error, rate limit, model refusal, empty text), the link is `active` with its fetched title and description, no summary/tags/topic, and a "re-run enrichment" action; the enrichment is retried once after 10 minutes automatically. A key the provider starts rejecting (revoked, out of credit) is reported once on the settings page as "your AI key was rejected: <provider message>" and enrichment pauses until the key is replaced; links added meanwhile wait in the unenriched state.
- Re-fetch (refresh) re-runs enrichment as well as the fetch, and keeps manual edits.

### Manual edits

- Manual edits win: a user can edit title, summary, tags and topic on the link detail view. A field a user has edited is never overwritten by later automatic enrichment or re-fetch.

### End-to-end flows

1. The owner enters an Anthropic API key in settings and sees "key verified", pastes `https://example.com/article?utm_source=x`, sees it at the top as `example.com` / pending; within a minute the card shows the title, summary, tags and topic.
2. The owner, without a key, pastes a link; it is fetched but not enriched and the stream shows the banner once; the owner adds a key, chooses "enrich all unenriched links", and the card gains its summary, tags and topic.
3. The owner edits a link's tags and topic, then refreshes it; the summary is renewed but the edited tags and topic stay.

## Design Decisions

1. **Enrichment runs on the Anthropic Claude API by default, with OpenRouter as the alternative provider**, chosen per user in settings together with the model; default model `claude-opus-5-5`. Owner's decision (source PRD decision 5).
2. **Bring your own key.** Enrichment never runs on a shared or deployment-wide key. Owner's decision (source PRD decision 9).
3. **Background processing is throttled to 20 links per minute per user** for imports and "enrich all". Owner's decision (source PRD decision 15). The throttle spaces a user's jobs 3 seconds apart by giving each queue message a delivery delay; a slot more than 12 hours ahead (the queue's longest delay) is sent with that delay and deferred again on arrival. Mechanism decided in this run: it needs no long-running process and keeps users independent.
4. **Enrichment runs on its own queue** (`ENRICH_QUEUE`, consumed by the enrichment worker): the fetch worker sends a message when a fetch makes a link `active` with text to enrich and the user has a verified key. Adding a single link or a paste is not throttled; only imports and "enrich all" are. Decided in this run, from the source PRD's 60-second goal for a pasted link.
5. **The key is encrypted with AES-GCM** under the deployment secret `KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, with a fresh IV per save and the user's id as additional authenticated data, so a ciphertext copied to another user's row does not decrypt. Decided in this run.
6. **The test request on save** is one minimal completion with the chosen model (a one-word answer); a provider that cannot be reached answers 502 `provider_unavailable` and nothing is stored. Decided in this run.
7. **A rejected key** is a provider answer of HTTP 401, 402 or 403 to an enrichment request. The key is marked `rejected` with the provider's message, the user's enrichment pauses, and the link (and every link reaching enrichment meanwhile) waits as `waiting_for_key`. Saving a key that verifies lifts the pause; waiting links are enriched by "enrich all unenriched links", as the source PRD says they wait. Decided in this run.
8. **The structured result.** The provider is asked for `{summary, tags, topic}` (Anthropic: a forced tool call; OpenRouter: a JSON-schema response format). Tags are lower-cased, spaces become hyphens, characters outside `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` are dropped, empties and repeats removed and the first 8 kept; the summary is cut to 60 words. A result with fewer than 3 tags, an empty summary or topic, or one that does not parse is an enrichment failure. Decided in this run: the source PRD fixes the bounds, not what to do when a model misses them.
9. **Converging vocabulary.** The request lists the user's topics (up to 100, most used first) and tags (up to 300, most used first); a returned name equal to an existing one ignoring case, with spaces read as hyphens, reuses it. Decided in this run, to bound the request size.
10. **Enrichment status** is one of `no_key`, `queued`, `enriched`, `failed`, `skipped` and `waiting_for_key`, shown on the link, so the owner always sees why a link has no summary. Decided in this run.
11. **Timeouts.** A provider call is abandoned after 60 seconds and counts as a failure. Decided in this run.
12. **Edit limits.** A title is 1 to 500 characters, a summary at most 2,000, at most 20 tags each normalised as above, a topic 1 to 100 characters. Editing a field records it as edited for good; there is no "revert to automatic" in this package. Decided in this run: the source PRD sets no limits.
13. **Test seam.** `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` default to the providers' and are pointed at `e2e/fake-ai.ts` in the end-to-end tests. Decided in this run.

## Dependencies

- Package 01 `accounts_links_and_stream` (draft): users, links, the settings page, the card and detail page, the API conventions and the test helpers.
- Package 02 `fetch_and_snapshot` (draft): the fetch worker, the reader-view text in `link_texts`, the notes that mark a link as having nothing to enrich, refresh, and the stream's change feed. This package changes the fetch worker so that a fetch sends an enrichment message and never overwrites an edited title.
- External: the Anthropic Claude API and OpenRouter, each called with the user's own key; Cloudflare Queues.

## Verified External API

Read from the published packages on 2026-11-07:

- `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 1.6.0: `new Anthropic({ apiKey, baseURL, ... }: ClientOptions)`; `client.messages.create(params: MessageCreateParamsNonStreaming, options?: RequestOptions): APIPromise<Message>`.
- `@openrouter/sdk` 1.5.64: `new OpenRouter(options?: SDKOptions)`; `client.chat.send(request: SendChatCompletionRequestRequest, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<SendChatCompletionRequestResponse>`. If the SDK does not run on Workers, OpenRouter's HTTP API (`POST /api/v1/chat/completions`) is the fallback.
- `hono` 4.13.17 and `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` 0.23.0 as in package 01.

## Glossary

- **enrichment**: the background step that produces summary, tags and topic.
- **topic**: the single automatically assigned category of a link; **tag**: one of several automatically or manually assigned labels.
- **AI key**: the user's own Anthropic or OpenRouter API key, stored for enrichment (bring your own key).
- **throttle**: the pacing of a user's background jobs, at most 20 per minute.
- **edited field**: a title, summary, tags or topic the owner has set by hand, which automatic work never overwrites.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: The owner's AI provider and key

**Rationale:** Enrichment spends the owner's money and sends the owner's pages, so it runs only on a key they chose and entered.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] WHEN a user requests PUT /api/v1/settings/ai with provider 'anthropic' or 'openrouter', a non-empty api_key and, for OpenRouter, a model, and the provider accepts a test request made with that key and model, THE Alexandria API SHALL store the provider, the model (claude-opus-5-5 when an Anthropic model is not given) and the key encrypted, replacing any previous settings, and mark the key verified
   → HTTP 200 with body {configured: true, provider, model, key_last4, status: 'verified', rejected_message: null}
   Check: unit
   - setup: the providers' endpoints answered by the fake AI provider of src/worker/test/ai.ts
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts, a table over {anthropic, key 'sk-ant-abcd1234', no model: model 'claude-opus-5-5'; openrouter, key 'sk-or-wxyz', model 'meta/llama-4': that model}: r = api('PUT', '/api/v1/settings/ai', {body}); assert r.status == 200 and r.json == {configured: true, provider, model, key_last4: last 4 of the key, status: 'verified', rejected_message: null}; assert the fake provider received exactly one test request carrying the key and model
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the provider rejects the test request made with the submitted key, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse to store the key, keeping any previous settings unchanged
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "key_rejected", "field": "api_key", "message": <the provider's error message>}; GET /api/v1/settings/ai returns what it returned before
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts, a table over {no previous key; a previous verified key}: the fake provider answers 401 {error: {message: 'invalid x-api-key'}}; r = PUT a new key; assert 400, error 'key_rejected', field 'api_key', message 'invalid x-api-key'; assert GET settings equals its earlier body
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] IF PUT /api/v1/settings/ai names a provider other than 'anthropic' or 'openrouter', has an empty or missing api_key, names OpenRouter without a model, or has a model longer than 200 characters, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the request without calling a provider and without storing anything
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "invalid_provider" | "invalid_key" | "model_required" | "invalid_model", "field", "message"}; the fake provider received no request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts, a table over {provider 'workers-ai': invalid_provider/provider; api_key '': invalid_key/api_key; no api_key: invalid_key/api_key; openrouter without model: model_required/model; model of 201 characters: invalid_model/model}: assert 400 with error and field; assert the fake provider's request log is empty and settings unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF the provider cannot be reached for the test request, answers with a 5xx status, or does not answer within 60 seconds, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse to store the key and say the provider is unavailable
   → HTTP 502 with body {"error": "provider_unavailable", "message": <text>}; settings unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts, a table over the fake provider {refusing connections; answering 529 overloaded; stalling past a 200 ms test timeout}: r = PUT; assert 502 and error 'provider_unavailable'; assert settings unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN a user requests GET /api/v1/settings/ai, THE Alexandria API SHALL return the stored provider, model, the key's last 4 characters, the key's status with the provider's rejection message when rejected, and the number of the user's links waiting to be enriched
   → HTTP 200 with body {configured: true, provider, model, key_last4, status: 'verified' | 'rejected', rejected_message, unenriched_count} or {configured: false, unenriched_count}
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts, a table over {no key and 2 links with enrichment_status 'no_key': {configured: false, unenriched_count: 2}; a verified key: configured true with key_last4; a key marked rejected with 'credit balance too low': status 'rejected' and that message}: assert GET /api/v1/settings/ai body
   ```
1. [REQ-1.6] WHEN a user requests DELETE /api/v1/settings/ai, THE Alexandria API SHALL remove the stored provider, model and key, so that later links are not enriched
   → HTTP 204; GET /api/v1/settings/ai then returns configured false; a link fetched afterwards gets enrichment_status 'no_key'
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts: save a key; assert DELETE answers 204; assert GET returns configured false and no ciphertext column is set; add a link and process its fetch; assert enrichment_status 'no_key' and the fake provider received no enrichment request
   ```
1. [REQ-1.7] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any stored key, keep it only encrypted with AES-GCM under KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY with the user's id bound as additional data, and never return the key, or any part of it beyond its last 4 characters, in any API response
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/keys.test.ts: save key 'sk-ant-secret-abcd1234'; assert no D1 value contains 'sk-ant-secret' or the whole key; assert decryptKey(ciphertext, iv, userId) == the key and decryptKey(ciphertext, iv, otherUserId) throws; and an afterAll hook over every response the shared api() helper recorded in the worker test run asserts that no body or header contains a saved test key
   ```
1. [REQ-1.8] WHEN the owner saves, replaces or removes the AI key on the settings page, THE website SHALL offer the provider choice with Anthropic preselected, the key and model inputs, show 'key verified' on success, the provider's message on a rejection, the stored key only as its last 4 characters, and Replace and Remove actions
   → after a successful save the page reads 'key verified' and '…1234'; on key_rejected it shows the provider's message; the key input is empty after any save
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx with a fake API: assert the provider select defaults to Anthropic and the model placeholder is 'claude-opus-5-5'; choose OpenRouter and assert the model input is required; save and assert 'key verified' and '…1234' and an empty key input; with the fake answering key_rejected assert its message is shown; click Remove and assert DELETE /api/v1/settings/ai
   ```

### REQ-2: Enriching a fetched link

**Rationale:** A summary, a few tags and one topic per link are what make a large library browsable at a glance.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a fetch or refresh makes a link 'active' with reader-view text or a title, and its user has a verified key, THE enrichment worker SHALL send an enrichment message for the link from the fetch worker, then call the user's provider with the user's key and model and store the summary, tags, topic and enrichment time on the link
   → GET /api/v1/links/{id} returns enrichment_status 'enriched', summary, tags: [string] (3 to 8), topic: string and enriched_at
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: save a key; the fake origin serves an article; add the link; process its fetch message, then the recorded ENRICH_QUEUE message, with the fake provider answering {summary: 'A short summary.', tags: ['cloudflare', 'queues', 'workers'], topic: 'web development'}; assert the link's enrichment_status 'enriched' and the three fields
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] THE enrichment worker SHALL for any enrichment request, send the provider only the instructions, the link's title and host, the user's existing topic and tag names, and the first 20,000 characters of the reader-view text, or the title and description when the reader view is empty; never the raw HTML, cookies, or the user's email, name or id
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over {an article whose reader text is 30,000 characters: the request holds exactly its first 20,000; a page with an empty reader view: the request holds the title and description and no page text}: enrich; take the fake provider's captured request body; assert the text part; assert it contains none of the snapshot's '<html', the owner's email, name or user id, and no cookie header was sent
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] THE enrichment worker SHALL for any tag or topic name returned by the provider, reuse the user's existing tag or topic whose name is equal ignoring case with spaces read as hyphens, and create a new one only when none is, listing the user's 100 most used topics and 300 most used tags in the request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table of (existing vocabulary, returned names, stored names, new rows): ({tag 'web-dev'}, ['Web Dev'], ['web-dev'], 0); ({topic 'Programming'}, topic 'programming', 'Programming', 0); ({}, ['rust'], ['rust'], 1); and with 400 existing tags assert the captured request lists exactly the 300 most used
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] THE enrichment worker SHALL for any provider result, lower-case the tags, turn spaces into hyphens, drop characters other than a-z, 0-9 and '-', drop empty and repeated tags, keep the first 8, and cut the summary to its first 60 words
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over normalizeResult inputs: tags ['Rust', 'rust', 'Web Assembly', 'C++', '', 'a', 'b', 'c', 'd', 'e', 'f'] -> ['rust', 'web-assembly', 'c', 'a', 'b', 'd', 'e', 'f']; a summary of 75 words -> its first 60 words; a summary of 60 words -> unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] IF a link is noted 'not a web page', 'no text in this PDF' or 'PDF too large to store (50 MB limit)', THEN THE enrichment worker SHALL send no enrichment message and call no provider for it
   → the link's enrichment_status is 'skipped'; no ENRICH_QUEUE message and no provider request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over the three notes, produced through the fake origin (an image, a scanned PDF, a 60 MB PDF), with a verified key: process the fetch; assert enrichment_status 'skipped', no recorded ENRICH_QUEUE message and an empty fake-provider log
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] THE enrichment worker SHALL for any user, call the provider only with that user's own key and model, and never with another user's key or a deployment-wide key
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: user A saves anthropic key kA, user B saves openrouter key kB with model mB; each adds a link; process all messages; assert the fake provider saw kA only on Anthropic requests for A's link and kB with mB only on OpenRouter requests for B's link
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] THE enrichment worker SHALL for any change of provider, model or key, leave the summary, tags and topic of already enriched links unchanged and send no enrichment for them
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: enrich a link; PUT a different provider and model; assert no ENRICH_QUEUE message was recorded and the link's summary, tags, topic and enriched_at are unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-2.8] THE enrichment worker SHALL for either provider, ask for the result as structured data, a forced tool call through the Anthropic Messages API or a JSON-schema response format through OpenRouter's chat completions, and read summary, tags and topic from it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/providers.test.ts, a table over {anthropic: the fake answers a tool_use block with input {summary, tags, topic}; openrouter: the fake answers a message whose content is that JSON}: r = enrichWith(provider, key, model, request); assert r == {summary, tags, topic}; assert the captured request named the model and carried tool_choice for Anthropic or response_format json_schema for OpenRouter
   ```

### REQ-4: The background throttle

**Rationale:** A large import or an 'enrich all' must not flood the provider, the owner's bill or the origin sites.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] THE background throttle SHALL for any job scheduled through the throttle for a user, give it a start time 3 seconds after that user's previous scheduled start, or the scheduling time when that slot has already passed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/throttle.test.ts: setNow(t); slots = scheduleThrottled(user, 600 jobs); assert slots[i] == t + 3 i seconds, so the last is t + 1797 s (under 30 minutes); setNow(t + 3 hours); assert the next scheduled slot == t + 3 hours
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] THE background throttle SHALL for any sequence of throttled scheduling calls for one user at any times, start at most 20 of the user's jobs in any 60-second window
   Check: property
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/throttle.test.ts: for random sequences of (time offset, batch size up to 200) calls: collect all slots; for every slot s assert count(slots in [s, s + 60 s)) <= 20 and every slot >= its call's time
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] THE background throttle SHALL for any two users, schedule their throttled jobs independently, so that one user's queued jobs never delay another user's
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/throttle.test.ts: schedule 600 jobs for A at t; schedule 1 job for B at t; assert B's slot == t
   ```
1. [REQ-4.4] IF a job's slot is more than 12 hours after the time its message is sent, THEN THE background throttle SHALL send the message with the queue's longest delay of 12 hours and, on its arrival before the slot, send it again for the time left instead of processing it
   → the first send carries delaySeconds 43200; a message arriving before its slot is re-sent with delaySeconds = slot - now and not processed; a message arriving at or after its slot is processed
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/throttle.test.ts: give a job a slot t + 14 h; assert the recorded send has delaySeconds 43200; deliver it at t + 12 h; assert it is re-sent with delaySeconds 7200 and the provider was not called; deliver it at t + 14 h; assert it is processed
   ```

### REQ-5: Enrichment failures and re-runs

**Rationale:** Providers fail and models refuse; the link must stay useful and the owner must be able to try again.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] IF the first automatic enrichment attempt of a link fails by a provider error other than a rejected key, a rate limit, a refusal, no answer within 60 seconds, or a result that is invalid after normalisation, THEN THE enrichment worker SHALL keep the link 'active' with its fetched title and description and no summary, tags or topic, mark it failed with the reason, and send the enrichment message again with a delay of 10 minutes
   → enrichment_status 'failed', enrichment_reason set, summary null, tags []; one ENRICH_QUEUE message re-sent with delaySeconds 600
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over the fake provider's answers {500; 429 with retry-after; a stop_reason 'refusal'; a stall past the test timeout; a result with 2 tags}: process the enrichment message; assert state 'active', the fetched title, enrichment_status 'failed', a reason, and one re-sent message with delaySeconds 600
   ```
1. [REQ-5.2] IF the automatic retry of a link's enrichment fails as well, THEN THE enrichment worker SHALL leave the link failed and send no further automatic retry
   → enrichment_status 'failed'; no ENRICH_QUEUE message sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts beside the test above: process the re-sent message with the fake still answering 500; assert enrichment_status 'failed' and no message recorded
   ```
1. [REQ-5.3] WHEN a user with a verified key requests POST /api/v1/links/{id}/enrich for one of their links that has reader-view text or a title to enrich, THE enrichment worker SHALL send an enrichment message for the link at once, outside the throttle, and mark it queued
   → HTTP 202 with body {status: 'queued'}; one ENRICH_QUEUE message with no delay; a later success stores the result as an automatic enrichment does
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: make a link 'failed'; the fake provider recovers; r = api('POST', '/api/v1/links/' + id + '/enrich'); assert 202 {status: 'queued'} and one message without delay; process it; assert enrichment_status 'enriched'
   ```
1. [REQ-5.4] IF POST /api/v1/links/{id}/enrich is requested without a verified key, or for a link that is 'pending', 'unreachable' or 'skipped', THEN THE enrichment worker SHALL refuse the request and send nothing
   → HTTP 409 with body {"error": "no_ai_key", "message": "add an AI key in settings"} without a verified key, or {"error": "nothing_to_enrich", "message": <text>} for such a link; no ENRICH_QUEUE message
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over {no key: no_ai_key; a 'pending' link: nothing_to_enrich; an 'unreachable' link: nothing_to_enrich; a 'skipped' PDF: nothing_to_enrich}: assert 409, the error code and no recorded message
   ```
1. [REQ-5.5] WHEN the stream or detail page shows a link whose enrichment_status is 'failed', THE website SHALL say 'enrichment failed' on its card with a 're-run enrichment' action that sends the enrich request
   → the card reads 'enrichment failed' and the action sends POST /api/v1/links/{id}/enrich, after which the card shows the queued state
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/components/LinkCard.test.tsx with a fake API: render a failed link; assert 'enrichment failed' and the 're-run enrichment' action; click it; assert one POST .../enrich and a queued indicator
   ```

### REQ-6: A key the provider starts rejecting

**Rationale:** A revoked or exhausted key must be reported once and stop the spending of failed requests, not fail every link one by one.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-6.1] IF the provider answers an enrichment request with HTTP 401, 402 or 403, THEN THE enrichment worker SHALL mark the user's key rejected with the provider's message, pause the user's enrichment, and leave the link waiting for a key without counting a failed attempt or retrying
   → GET /api/v1/settings/ai returns status 'rejected' and rejected_message equal to the provider's message; the link's enrichment_status is 'waiting_for_key'; no ENRICH_QUEUE message is re-sent
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts, a table over the fake provider's {401 'invalid x-api-key'; 402 'insufficient credits'; 403 'permission denied'}: process an enrichment message; assert the settings status and message, the link's 'waiting_for_key' and no re-sent message
   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHILE the user's key is marked rejected, THE enrichment worker SHALL mark every link of the user that reaches enrichment as waiting for a key without calling the provider
   → such links get enrichment_status 'waiting_for_key'; the fake provider receives no request
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: mark the key rejected; add two links and process their fetch and enrichment messages; assert both 'waiting_for_key' and an empty fake-provider log
   ```
1. [REQ-6.3] WHEN the user saves a key that the provider accepts while the previous key is marked rejected, THE enrichment worker SHALL replace the key and lift the pause, leaving the waiting links waiting until the owner chooses 'enrich all unenriched links'
   → GET /api/v1/settings/ai returns status 'verified' and rejected_message null; links added afterwards are enriched; waiting links keep 'waiting_for_key' and are counted in unenriched_count
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: with a rejected key and one waiting link, PUT a key the fake accepts; assert status 'verified'; add a new link and assert it ends 'enriched'; assert the waiting link is still 'waiting_for_key' and unenriched_count == 1
   ```
1. [REQ-6.4] WHILE the owner's key is marked rejected, THE website SHALL show 'your AI key was rejected: <provider message>' once at the top of the settings page, beside the Replace and Remove actions, until the key is replaced or removed
   → the settings page shows the message exactly once; no card carries it
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/pages/Settings.test.tsx with a fake API answering status 'rejected' and 'insufficient credits': assert 'your AI key was rejected: insufficient credits' appears once; with status 'verified' assert it is absent; in src/web/pages/Stream.test.tsx assert no card shows it
   ```

### REQ-7: Manual edits win

**Rationale:** The owner's own words about a link are worth more than any model's, and must never be silently undone.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-7.1] WHEN a user requests PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} for one of their links with any of title, summary, tags and topic, each valid, THE Alexandria API SHALL store the given fields and record each of them as edited
   → HTTP 200 with body <link> carrying the new values and edited_fields listing the given fields together with those edited before
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts: r = api('PATCH', '/api/v1/links/' + id, {body: {tags: ['Reading List', 'rust'], topic: 'Programming'}}); assert 200, tags == ['reading-list', 'rust'], topic 'Programming' and edited_fields == ['tags', 'topic']; PATCH {title: 'My title'}; assert edited_fields == ['tags', 'topic', 'title']
   ```
1. [REQ-7.2] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any field a user has edited, leave it unchanged through every later automatic enrichment, re-run enrichment and refresh, while still updating the fields not edited
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts, a table over edited field {title, summary, tags, topic} crossed with {automatic enrichment after a refresh, POST .../enrich}: edit the field; the fake origin and fake provider now answer different values; run the operation through its messages; assert the edited field keeps the owner's value and the other three fields took the new automatic values
   ```
1. [REQ-7.3] IF PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} carries a title that is empty or longer than 500 characters, a summary longer than 2,000 characters, tags that are not a list of at most 20 names each non-empty after normalisation, or a topic that is empty or longer than 100 characters, THEN THE Alexandria API SHALL refuse the whole request and change nothing
   → HTTP 400 with body {"error": "invalid_title" | "invalid_summary" | "invalid_tags" | "invalid_topic", "field", "message"}; the link and its edited_fields are unchanged
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts, a table over bodies {title '': invalid_title; title of 501 chars: invalid_title; summary of 2,001 chars: invalid_summary; tags 'rust': invalid_tags; 21 tags: invalid_tags; tags ['++']: invalid_tags; topic '': invalid_topic; topic of 101 chars: invalid_topic; {title: 'ok', topic: ''}: invalid_topic}: assert 400, error, field; assert the link unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-7.4] THE Alexandria API SHALL for any edited tag or topic name, normalise it as provider tags are normalised and reuse the user's existing tag or topic of the same name ignoring case, creating one only when none exists
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/edits.test.ts, a table of (existing vocabulary, edit, stored, new rows): ({tag 'web-dev'}, tags ['Web Dev'], ['web-dev'], 0); ({topic 'Programming'}, topic 'PROGRAMMING', 'Programming', 0); ({}, tags ['zig'], ['zig'], 1): PATCH; assert stored names and the count of new tag or topic rows
   ```
1. [REQ-7.5] WHEN the owner edits title, summary, tags or topic on a link's detail page, THE website SHALL offer in-place editing of the four fields, send only the changed fields, show the saved values and mark edited fields as set by the owner
   → one PATCH /api/v1/links/{id} carrying only the changed fields; each edited field shows an 'edited' marker; a 400 shows its message beside the field
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/pages/LinkDetail.test.tsx with a fake API: edit the topic and save; assert one PATCH with body {topic: 'Rust'} only; assert the topic shows 'Rust' with an 'edited' marker; with the fake answering 400 invalid_topic assert the message is shown beside the topic
   ```

### REQ-8: Showing summary, tags and topic

**Rationale:** Enrichment is only worth its cost if the owner sees it where they browse.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN a client reads a link through GET /api/v1/links, GET /api/v1/links/{id} or the change feed, THE Alexandria API SHALL include the link's summary, tags, topic, enrichment status, enrichment reason and edited fields
   → every link object carries summary: string | null, tags: [string], topic: string | null, enrichment_status, enrichment_reason: string | null, edited_fields: [string]
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/worker/enrich/enrich.test.ts: enrich a link; for each of GET /api/v1/links, GET /api/v1/links/{id} and GET /api/v1/links?changed_since=t0 assert the link object carries the six fields with the enriched values
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] WHEN the stream shows an enriched link, THE website SHALL show its summary in two lines that expand on request, its tags and its topic
   → the card shows the summary clamped to two lines with a 'more' control that expands it, one chip per tag and the topic
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/components/LinkCard.test.tsx: render a link with a 60-word summary, tags ['rust', 'wasm', 'performance'] and topic 'Programming'; assert the summary element is clamped to two lines, clicking 'more' removes the clamp, three tag chips and the topic are shown
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHILE the stream page holds a card whose enrichment_status is 'queued', or whose link is pending with a verified key, THE website SHALL keep asking for changed links every 5 seconds, so that summary, tags and topic appear on the card without a reload
   → changed_since requests continue while such a card remains; the card shows the summary once the feed returns it; requests stop when none remains
   Check: unit
   ```
   in src/web/pages/Stream.test.tsx with fake timers: render an 'active' card with enrichment_status 'queued'; advance 5 s; assert one changed_since request; the fake returns it 'enriched' with a summary; assert the summary on the same card; advance 15 s; assert no further request
   ```

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: The owner adds a key and a pasted link is enriched within a minute

1. **owner** chooses Anthropic on the settings page, enters an API key and saves
2. **Alexandria API** sends a test request with the key to the AI provider
3. **AI provider** accepts the test request
4. **Alexandria API** stores the key encrypted and answers verified
5. **website** shows 'key verified' and the key's last 4 characters
6. **owner** pastes 'https://example.com/article?utm_source=x' and presses Enter
7. **fetch worker** fetches the page, stores its snapshot and reader view, sets the link 'active' and sends an enrichment message
8. **enrichment worker** sends the reader text and the vocabulary to the AI provider with the owner's key and model
9. **AI provider** returns a summary, tags and a topic
10. **enrichment worker** normalises the result, reuses or creates tags and the topic, and stores them on the link
11. **website** shows the title, summary, tags and topic on the card without a reload

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, FETCH_QUEUE, fetch worker, ENRICH_QUEUE, enrichment worker, key encryption, R2 bucket SNAPSHOTS, D1 database, @anthropic-ai/sdk client

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local bindings and KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY set
- ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL points at e2e/fake-ai.ts, which accepts the key 'sk-ant-test-1234' and answers enrichment with a fixed summary, tags and topic; ORIGIN_PROXY_URL points at e2e/fake-origin.ts playing https://example.com/article (the provider and the origin are the only stubbed parties besides e2e/fake-google.ts)
- the owner signed in with no key

**End state:**

- the settings page showed 'key verified' and '…1234'
- within 60 seconds of Enter, without a reload, the card shows the fetched title, the fake's summary, its tags and its topic
- the users row holds no plaintext key; the fake provider received the key only in its authentication header
- the fake provider's enrichment request contained the article text and not the owner's email

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/enrichment.spec.ts: sign in; on /settings choose Anthropic, enter 'sk-ant-test-1234', save; expect 'key verified' and '…1234'; on / paste the URL and press Enter; expect within 60 s the first card's summary, tags and topic to equal the fake's, with the navigation count unchanged; assert fakeAi.requests' body contains the article's first sentence and not 'owner@example.test'
```

### PATH-2: Links added without a key are enriched after the owner adds one

1. **owner** pastes two URLs without having stored a key
2. **fetch worker** fetches and snapshots both and marks them not enriched for want of a key
3. **website** shows 'not enriched: add an AI key in settings' once above the stream
4. **owner** saves an OpenRouter key and model on the settings page and chooses 'Enrich all unenriched links (2)'
5. **Alexandria API** schedules both links through the background throttle and answers 'queued 2 links'
6. **enrichment worker** enriches each link with the owner's OpenRouter key and model when its slot comes
7. **website** drops the banner and shows summaries, tags and topics on both cards

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, fetch worker, background throttle, ENRICH_QUEUE, enrichment worker, D1 database, OpenRouter client

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local bindings; OPENROUTER_BASE_URL points at e2e/fake-ai.ts; ORIGIN_PROXY_URL at e2e/fake-origin.ts serving two articles; the owner signed in with no key

**End state:**

- before the key, both cards had titles and no summaries, and exactly one banner was shown
- the settings page reported 'queued 2 links'
- the second enrichment request reached the fake provider at least 3 seconds after the first
- both cards show summaries, tags and topics and the banner is gone

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/enrichment.spec.ts: sign in; paste two URLs; expect both cards 'active' and one banner; on /settings save an OpenRouter key with model 'test/model'; click 'Enrich all unenriched links (2)'; expect 'queued 2 links'; expect both cards' summaries within 60 s; assert fakeAi.requests timestamps differ by >= 3 s and the banner is absent
```

### PATH-3: The owner's edits survive a refresh

1. **owner** edits an enriched link's tags and topic on its detail page
2. **Alexandria API** stores them and records tags and topic as edited
3. **owner** chooses Refresh on the link
4. **fetch worker** fetches the changed page, replaces the snapshot, keeps edited fields and sends an enrichment message
5. **enrichment worker** stores the new summary and leaves the edited tags and topic untouched
6. **website** shows the new summary with the owner's tags and topic

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** website, Alexandria API, fetch worker, enrichment worker, D1 database

**Setup:**

- wrangler dev with local bindings; e2e/fake-ai.ts and e2e/fake-origin.ts as above, both switched to new answers after the edit; a verified key and an enriched link

**End state:**

- the link's tags and topic are the owner's values and edited_fields lists them
- its summary is the fake provider's second summary
- the card shows both

**Pseudocode:**

```
in e2e/enrichment.spec.ts: on the detail page set tags 'mine' and topic 'Mine'; switch the fakes to new answers; click Refresh; expect within 60 s the new summary while tags read 'mine' and topic 'Mine'; GET the link and assert edited_fields contains 'tags' and 'topic'
```
